# Coconut

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="coconut-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="coconut-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="coconut-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Maduagwuna · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/famurewa2023-coconut-oil-metals-pesticides">Comparative assessment of different coconut oils: Chromatographic and spectrometric analyses of pesticide residues, toxic heavy metals, and associated contents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Measurement: Food</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/famurewa2023-coconut-oil-metals-pesticides">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Inna V. Kharin · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Integral assessment of the environmental safety of plant-based milk alternatives based on heavy metal analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Izvestiya KGTU (KSTU News)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Coconut, oil from unrefined had lead higher at 2.09 µg/kg, against 0.681 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/famurewa2023-coconut-oil-metals-pesticides|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ademola C. Maduagwuna · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/famurewa2023-coconut-oil-metals-pesticides">Comparative assessment of different coconut oils: Chromatographic and spectrometric analyses of pesticide residues, toxic heavy metals, and associated contents</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Measurement: Food</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/famurewa2023-coconut-oil-metals-pesticides">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Higher results came from contaminated or exposed settings rather than ordinary supply. Coconut, oil from unrefined had Mn higher at 46.7 µg/kg, against 2.88 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the coconut came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as coconut

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-coconut" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-coconut-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of coconut, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach coconut

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach coconut comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Coconut, oil from unrefined had Mn higher at 46.7 µg/kg, against 2.88 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-coconut" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-coconut" data-question="What heavy metals are found in coconut?">

In the studies available, coconut from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than coconut from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Coconut, oil from unrefined had lead higher at 2.09 µg/kg, against 0.681 µg/kg for refined in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Lin S-T, Liao K-W, Xuan T-C, Chiou T-Y, Lin Z-E, Lee W-J · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Determination, distribution, and health risk assessment of 12 heavy metals in various edible oils in Taiwan</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">JSFA Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lin2024-edible-oils-taiwan-12-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-coconut" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-coconut" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in coconut?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in coconut?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, coconut, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (10 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (20 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (14.1 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (18.1 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-coconut" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-coconut" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in coconut?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in coconut?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same coconut.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Coconut, oil (GEMS/Food contaminants database) had cadmium lower at 5.3 µg/kg, against 8.5 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (coconut, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-coconut-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-coconut-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in coconut is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in coconut is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 5.2 µg/kg (mean) in coconut, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
